newsitem.title: FRANCE: Supply pressure hits French maize prices.
newsitem.headline: Supply pressure hits French maize prices.

text.p: French maize prices slipped on Tuesday as grain cooperatives turned sellers amid prospects of a bumper crop, dealers said.
Maize into Bordeaux was paid at 830 francs per tonne for November delivery and 840 francs on December-January delivery, both down 10 francs on Monday.
Dealers said the latest data coming from key production areas in the southwest suggested higher-than-expected yields.
On Monday crop analysts in the Aquitaine region revised upwards their estimate for yields to a record 9.3-9.4 tonnes from a pre-harvest estimate of 8.6 tonnes.
In the Landes area, average yields may hit a record 10.3-10.5 tonnes per hectare against 9.9 tonnes last year, dealers said.
Last week the French farm ministry revised upwards its estimate for the national maize crop to 13.97 million tonnes from its October target of 13.78 million and 12.7 million produced in 1995.
But industry sources said the final tally may be even higher.
"We are now targeting a crop of 14.2 million tonnes," one dealer said.
